name: Modbus Frame Builder
blurb: an RTU/TCP frame with its CRC from function code and registers
intro: Builds a Modbus request from the function code, slave, start address and values: the PDU per the Modbus Application Protocol, wrapped as RTU (with CRC-16, low byte first), ASCII (with LRC) or TCP (with the MBAP header). It also gives the expected response length and, for serial, the time on the wire and the t3.5 gap.

inputs.label: Values (writes)
inputs.help: Comma or space separated: registers as decimal, -signed or 0x hex; coils as 1/0/on/off.

examples.title: Read 2 holding registers from slave 1 (spec: 01 03 00 00 00 02 C4 0B)
Write 3 registers over TCP to unit 17 at 40108

usage: Give mode (rtu, tcp or ascii), slave id 0–247, function code fc (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 15, 16), addrStyle pdu (0-based as sent) or plc (40001 = holding register 0), the start address, the quantity for reads and a comma-separated values list for writes, plus tid for TCP and baud for serial. Returns the frame in hex, a field-by-field table, the CRC or LRC, the expected response length and wire times, and the frame as a C array and Python bytes. Use it to build a test request or to check a device's frames byte for byte.
sources: Modbus Application Protocol Specification V1.1b3, §6 (function codes 01–06, 15, 16)
Modbus over Serial Line Specification V1.02, §2.5 (RTU/ASCII framing, t3.5), §6.2 (CRC and LRC)
Modbus Messaging on TCP/IP Implementation Guide V1.0b, §3.1.3 (MBAP header)
